page: Microsoft Azure D48_v4 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the Dv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes hyper-threading with 2.0 threads per core. Memory capacity is 192.0 GB, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the middle 50% tier. Single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core results categorized in the bottom 25% (weak). However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is strong, placing in the top 25% for both read and write operations. Other operations, such as static web serving throughput, Redis SET operations, and Passmark database operations, consistently perform in the average tier. Large-model LLM text generation is a weakness, with text generation speeds for small and medium models falling into the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D48_v4 offers a standard resource density for general-purpose workloads that require substantial memory and multi-threaded processing without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The lack of local storage means storage-heavy operations must rely on external network-attached storage. This server is suited for multi-threaded decompression tasks, general database operations, web serving, and software compilation, but is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or real-time LLM text generation.
